screens.prompt: In B7, return the product name for the SKU in B6, even though the name column sits left of the key.

hints.syntax: =XLOOKUP(B6,B2:B5,A2:A5): the searched column first, the answer column second.
hints.func-xlookup: The name sits left of the SKU, which is the case XLOOKUP handles without help.
hints.require-ref: Take the SKU from B6, so the next question is one edit away.
hints.value: DX-410 is the third SKU down, so the answer is the third name in the column to its left.
hints.error: A SKU that is not in B2:B5 returns #N/A. The grader says the same when the search column holds product names.

docs.explain:
Four functions do this job: VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, INDEX with MATCH, and XLOOKUP. VLOOKUP reads right from the key column and HLOOKUP reads down from the key row. INDEX with MATCH reaches either way, at the cost of two functions.

This sheet puts the product name left of the SKU, which is the case that separates them. VLOOKUP cannot return a column left of its first column. XLOOKUP names B2:B5 to search and A2:A5 to return, and the leftward move costs nothing.

Choose by where the answer sits. Right of the key, VLOOKUP is one function and one number. Left of it, XLOOKUP names the column without counting.

errors.text: Nothing in the searched column matched, so the lookup has no row to return from.
A VLOOKUP column number counted past the returned range, so it points at a column that is not there.

docs.atWork: A stock file exported by a till, where the code sits to the right of a description nobody wants to retype.
docs.outcome: Pick the lookup that can return a column to the left of its key.

seo.title: Which Excel lookup should you use?
seo.description: VLOOKUP and HLOOKUP only return what sits right of its key. INDEX with MATCH goes anywhere in two functions, and XLOOKUP names both columns.
